notice: SYNTHETIC HELD-OUT ENGINEERING SET. Every document, passage, number and question below was written for this repository in M11, after the entire M0-M10 pipeline was committed at e0ee0ad. Nothing here influenced any threshold, policy or prompt, because all of them were frozen before these cases existed. That is the only sense in which this set is held out: it is not a held-out sample of any real population, it was authored by the same engineer who ran it, and no clinician reviewed it. The content is deliberately fictional and must never be read as medical guidance.

chunks.label: h-zolamine-basic
chunks.text: Zolamine is a fictional agent used only in this evaluation corpus. It is eliminated by the invented hepatic enzyme synthase Q, and its illustrative maintenance dose in this fictional text is 40 mg once daily.

chunks.label: h-zolamine-enzyme
chunks.text: Synthase Q, the invented enzyme of this corpus, is strongly inhibited by the fictional compound mirabex. Agents cleared by synthase Q therefore accumulate when mirabex is co-administered.

chunks.label: h-negation
chunks.text: In this fictional corpus, zolamine is not recommended for use with mirabex. The combination is described as contraindicated because of the accumulation caused by synthase Q inhibition.

chunks.label: h-fragment
chunks.text: the remainder of the fictional discussion continues on the following page and is not reproduced here

chunks.label: h-table-dose
chunks.text: Table H.1 Illustrative dosing of fictional agents. Agent | Illustrative adult dose | Interval. Zolamine | 40 mg | once daily. Perivane | 250 mg | twice daily. Corbastat | 10 mg | once daily.

chunks.label: h-formula-clearance
chunks.text: Fictional clearance index = (dose in mg x 3) / (weight in kg), where dose is the illustrative daily dose and weight is the recorded body weight in kilograms.

chunks.label: h-figure-curve

chunks.label: h-guide-b-agree

cases.category: known limitation: disagreeing values phrased differently
cases.question: What illustrative infusion rate does this corpus give?
cases.note: MEASURED LIMITATION, NOT A TARGET. The M7 conflict detector compares values only when the four-word label window preceding the number matches between sources. These two sources state different values for the same fictional quantity but phrase it differently, so the gate does not see a conflict and returns SUFFICIENT. The abstention here comes from M8 refusing the draft, not from M7 detecting the disagreement, and M8 reports the disagreement with the same AUTHORITATIVE_SOURCES_DISAGREE code the gate would have used. Attribution therefore points at SUFFICIENCY, which is the useful reading: the gate is where this should have been caught. The expectation records what the system actually does, so the gap is visible in every report rather than discovered later.
